earlier_scan.source_named: Oates, W.J. & Oates, L.F. 1958. The phonemes of Central Cagayan Negrito. Oceania Linguistic Monographs 3.
earlier_scan.note: Healey 1960 An Agta Grammar (read on archive.org) gives phonemes + vowel length but no stress statement; Oates phonemes paper not online

sources.citation: Healey, Phyllis M. 1960. An Agta Grammar. Manila: Summer Institute of Linguistics / Institute of National Language (Bureau of Printing). vi+103 pp. [open scan on archive.org as rosettaproject_dgc_book-1, misfiled by Rosetta under Casiguran dgc; describes Central Cagayan Agta]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (archive.org lending); also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number OC.IND. H 349 a) (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number OC.IND. H 349 a
sources.note: Sec. 0.5 Phonology (p. 3) lists phonemes and states 'Phonemic vowel length, represented by (´), occurs with the vowels a, i, and u, but not e and o'; length written with an acute in all examples (bakbákat, báhuy, pirák); morphophonemic 'shifting of vowel length' noted (p. 9, p. 33). No statement anywhere of where stress falls (0 hits for stress/accent/penult in full scanned).

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1979. On the development of contrastive word accent: Pangasinan, a case in point / Proto-Philippine word accent (PL, scanned held for cent2091); Zorc 1993 Overview of Austronesian and Philippine accent patterns (held for mara1404)
sources.note: Zorc 1979 cites one Agta form (qaddu 'many') in a gemination argument; neither paper classifies Central Cagayan Agta's accent type.
No lect/inventory for Central Cagayan Agta in either database (StressTyp2 only has the Ethnologue code row; phoible.org/languages/cent2084 = 404).

sources.citation: Mayfield, Roy. 1987. Central Cagayan Agta Texts. Studies in Philippine Linguistics, Supplementary Series: Philippine Texts 2. Manila: LSP & SIL. (Rosetta Project excerpts: phonology paragraph, ethnographic intro, glossed text 1)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.95.53.1.2 (2))
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.95.53.1.2 (2)
sources.note: Phoneme paragraph lists segmental phonemes (incl. two central vowels, glottal stop) and says nothing about stress or length; practical orthography in the texts carries no accent marks. Appendix C (morphophonemics) not in the open excerpt.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason W. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD diss., U Hawai'i. Sec. 3.2.16 'Central Cagayan Agta' (p. 89-90).
sources.note: Bibliographic paragraph only (Healey 1960, Mayfield 1987, NT 1992, SIL literacy PDFs); no phonology.

sources.citation: Robinson, Laura C. 2011. Dupaningan Agta: Grammar, vocabulary and texts. Pacific Linguistics 635. (held held by the project for dupa1235)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5662 .R62 2012
sources.note: Mentions Central Cagayan (Labin) Agta only for the *r/*h merger (citing Oates & Oates 1958) and loans; nothing on its stress. Different language (dupa1235).

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 2009. On the diachronic development of C1V1- reduplication in some Austronesian languages. Morphology 19: 239-261 (author version, UH ScholarSpace 10125/33040).
sources.note: Cites Central Cagayan Agta C1a- reduplication (Healey 1960 p. 9) and Oates & Oates 1955 vocabulary forms; no statement about CCA stress.

sources.citation: Liao, Hsiu-chuan. 2004. Transitivity and ergativity in Formosan and Philippine languages. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Ch. 6 'Transitivity and ergativity in Central Cagayan Agta', pp. 359ff.
sources.note: Syntax only; fn. 3 p. 361 adopts Mayfield 1987 orthography (two central vowels, glottal stop in clusters); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1973. Diachronic typology of Philippine vowel systems. In T. Sebeok (ed.), Current Trends in Linguistics 11: 485-506. (author version, UH ScholarSpace 10125/32977)
sources.note: Sec. 3.4.2: 'One analysis (Oates 1958) considered a and ʌ to be allophones, ʌ occurring in unstressed syllables, a elsewhere. In an unpublished subsequent analysis, Mayfield (1964) disagrees..' -- only an indirect pointer; no statement of stress position. Bibliography confirms Oates & Oates 1958 pp. 34-46 and Mayfield 1964 ms. 'The phonemes of Central Cagayan Agta' (SIL Philippines files).
